results.fact: Gain vs loss on a loop that ends at the trailhead
results.evidence: Retry found no new car-to-car figure for this 4-day Easy Ridge in / Whatcom Pass out loop. The 2011 account of exactly this loop gives 37 mi and 13,700 ft gained and lost; the speed-record page gives 12,000 ft of gain; a 2022 party that went in and out via Easy Ridge (a different shape, plus Challenger) reports 44 mi and 18,000 ft. No two sources agree on a total for this loop. What would settle it: a second independent account of the same loop stating its total gain/loss.

South-side ascents are documented on 3 Aug 2014 (south snowfield soft, no crampons needed), in mid-August (speed record), and on 21-24 July 2022 and 28-31 July 2011 (good snow cover); a late-August 2017 ranger party was turned back by a moat. The August ascents weaken 'August risky', but no source rates months or states whether September belongs in the working window, so rewriting the month breakdown would be a judgement, not a sourced fact. What would settle it: a source that characterises typical south-side conditions by month, or dated September ascents.

results.fact: Day 1 elevation loss (300 ft over Hannegan Pass to the Chilliwack ford)
results.evidence: One account records 4,700 ft gained and 2,700 ft lost from the trailhead to camp on Easy Ridge; a 2022 account says only that the trail below Hannegan Pass loses a 'deceptively large' amount of elevation, with no figure. Day 1 lossFt (300) is clearly too low, but changing it alone would break the itinerary's agreement with loss_ft (9,300), and no two sources state a car-to-car loss for this loop. What would settle it: a second source for the day-1 figures together with a sourced loop total.

results.correct_value: Pitch 3 is 5.9 and runout; its letter rating is given as PG-13 in one account and R in another, so both fields state 'runout' without a letter.
results.evidence: The first-ascent write-up rates pitch 3 '5.9 PG-13, 200 ft'; the route database page rates it '5.9R 200'' with the same description (knifeblade before the slab step, friable discontinuous corners, fixed #1 KB at the belay). The expedition report in the AAJ gives no protection letter. Both rated sources agree the pitch is 5.9 and runout; they disagree only on the letter, so the row now says runout in both places and no longer asserts either letter.

Hannegan Pass sits at about 5,066 ft and the Brush Creek trail low point near the Chilliwack at about 2,700 ft, so the day's note (drop ~2,500 ft) is plausible and lossFt 1,700 / gainFt 3,600 look too low. But no source states this day's totals, and changing them would move the itinerary off gain_ft/loss_ft (7,700 each), which no source states either. What would settle it: an account of the Hannegan-to-Whatcom Pass day stating its gain and loss plus a sourced round-trip total.

Two independent August ascents are now documented: 7 Aug 2022 up the North Ridge from Whatcom Pass in running shoes, skirting all the snow on the right, rock solid enough; and 3 Aug 2014, descending the North Ridge, where a snow patch on the ridge caused a fall. They show August is climbable but disagree on how the snow behaves, and no source addresses September. What would settle it: dated September ascents or a source rating the months for this ridge.
